Usage: openwop analytics summary [--days 7|30|90] [--json] openwop analytics events [--days 7|30|90] [--json] openwop analytics collect --session [--type ] [--path

] [--name ] [--prop k=v]... [--json] openwop analytics rollup [--json] openwop analytics trend --days [--json] openwop analytics nav report [--json] openwop analytics nav record --route --source Every write also accepts --body / --body-file for the full request body (typed flags override it). Endpoints: trend GET /v1/host/openwop-app/analytics/orgs/:orgId/trend Daily pageviews / events / conversions / uniques over the window. nav report GET /v1/host/openwop-app/analytics/nav/report Workspace navigation telemetry: which routes people reach, and from where (last 6 weeks). nav record POST /v1/host/openwop-app/analytics/nav Record one navigation (202; invalid or capped input is dropped, not rejected). Org-scoped usage analytics (ADR 0018 host extension). Aliased as `usage`. Endpoints: GET /v1/host/openwop-app/analytics/orgs/:orgId/summary aggregate usage rollup [authed, workspace:read] GET /v1/host/openwop-app/analytics/orgs/:orgId/events recent raw events (max 100) [authed, workspace:read] POST /v1/host/openwop-app/public-analytics/:orgId/collect record one event [PUBLIC, unauthed] GET /v1/host/openwop-app/usage/orgs/:orgId/rollup AI token usage + cost estimate per provider/model [authed, host:members:manage, toggle 'usage-analytics'] (a model with no known rate shows cost '?' — never a fabricated 0) This is USAGE / cost / observability — distinct from `governance audit` (the policy-decision log). The HOST is the authority: it aggregates server-side and gates each org read by RBAC (workspace:read) + the org-tenant's `analytics` toggle. This command only RENDERS what the host returns; it never computes a rollup locally. When analytics isn't served the host returns a uniform 404 and the command fails closed legibly (exit 2). The public `collect` beacon is consent-gated host-side (ADR 0020): a 201 records the event; a 202 means analytics consent wasn't granted (honestly reported, not recorded). It is sent WITHOUT auth (public path) — no bearer is attached. --session (collect) The visitor session key (== the consent subject key). Required. --type (collect) Event type: pageview | event | conversion (host default: event). --path

(collect) Page path (for pageviews). --name (collect) Event name. --prop k=v (collect) A typed property (repeatable; v parsed as number/bool/string). --json Emit the raw host JSON. Exit codes: 0 ok · 1 host error · 2 usage error / analytics not served / not authorized. Examples: openwop analytics summary org_123 openwop usage events org_123 --json openwop analytics collect org_123 --session s_abc --type pageview --path /pricing openwop usage rollup org_123

help.stdout:
Usage:
  openwop approvals list [--status pending|approved|rejected] [--json]
  openwop approvals get <approvalId> [--json]
  openwop approvals claim <approvalId> [--note <text>] [--acted-for <subject>] [--expected-hash <h>] [--json]
  openwop approvals reject <approvalId> [--note <text>] [--acted-for <subject>] [--expected-hash <h>] [--json]
  openwop approvals sla-policy [--json]
  openwop approvals sla-policy set (--enabled | --disabled) [--remind-after-ms n] [--escalate-after-ms n] [--expire-after-ms n] [--json]
  openwop approvals email-pref [--json]
  openwop approvals email-pref set --email <addr> (--enabled | --disabled) [--json]
  openwop approvals delegations list [--all] [--json]
  openwop approvals delegations create --to <subject> --starts-at <iso> --ends-at <iso> [--from <subject>] [--reason <t>] [--json]
  openwop approvals delegations revoke <delegationId> [--json]

The approval inbox — the human side of "agents propose, humans dispose". A
review-mode roster member's heartbeat queues a proposal instead of starting the
run; these commands let a human resolve it. A CLAIM is the affirmative act: it
starts the proposed run (replay/fork/observability inherited). A REJECT dismisses
the proposal so the heartbeat won't re-propose it.

The host is the authority for every decision — the CLI renders the host's
resolved queue and relays your claim/reject; it never decides locally. If the
host does not advertise the approval surface (/.well-known/openwop), the group
fails closed rather than guessing.

Endpoints:
  list    GET  /v1/host/openwop-app/approvals[?status=...]
  get     GET  /v1/host/openwop-app/approvals   (filtered to <approvalId> client-side;
          the host exposes no single-approval GET)
  claim   POST /v1/host/openwop-app/approvals/{id}/claim
  reject  POST /v1/host/openwop-app/approvals/{id}/reject
  sla-policy        GET/PUT /v1/host/openwop-app/approvals/sla-policy (ADR 0478; the tenant's
                    remind → escalate → expire timers. PUT needs an admin role — exit 4 otherwise.
                    'set' reads the current policy first and sends it back with your changes.)
  email-pref        GET/PUT /v1/host/openwop-app/approvals/email-pref (your own opt-in to decide
                    approvals from email; needs a signed-in user)
  delegations       GET/POST /v1/host/openwop-app/approval-delegations and
                    POST …/approval-delegations/{id}/revoke (ADR 0198; you delegate YOUR
                    approvals to someone for a window; --all and --from are operator-only)

  --acted-for <s>      (claim/reject) As a delegate covering several people, whose approval this is.
  --expected-hash <h>  (claim/reject) The definition hash you reviewed (composed-workflow proposals;
                       the host refuses the decision if the proposal changed since).
  --status <s>   (list) Filter the queue: pending | approved | rejected (default: all).
  --note <text>  (claim/reject) Optional human note recorded with the decision.
  --json         Print the raw host response instead of the rendered view.

Boundary: this is NOT `interrupts`. Interrupts are run-level HITL tokens you
resolve to resume a paused run; approvals are the policy-gated proposal queue.

Exit codes (get/claim/reject reflect the approval's resulting status, so scripts
can gate on the verdict):
  0  approved        3  pending        1  rejected (denied) or error
`list` exits 0 on success.

Examples:
  openwop approvals list --status pending
  openwop approvals get appr_123 --json
  openwop approvals claim appr_123 --note "LGTM, ship it"
  openwop approvals reject appr_123 --note "out of policy"

Teams approval delivery:
  openwop approvals teams-pref [--json]
  openwop approvals teams-pref set --connection-id <connectionId> --chat-id <chatId>
  openwop approvals teams-pref clear

Every write also accepts --body <json> / --body-file <path> for the full request body (typed flags override it).

Endpoints:
  teams-pref                   GET    /v1/host/openwop-app/approval-delivery/teams
                               Where your approval requests are delivered in Teams (null = not set).
  teams-pref set               PUT    /v1/host/openwop-app/approval-delivery/teams
                               Deliver your approval requests to a Teams chat through one of your connections.
  teams-pref clear             DELETE /v1/host/openwop-app/approval-delivery/teams
                               Stop Teams delivery of your approval requests.

Usage:
  openwop bi metrics <orgId> [--json]
  openwop bi metrics get <orgId> <metricId> [--json]
  openwop bi metrics create <orgId> --metric-id <metricId> --title <title> --entity-type <entityType> --aggregate <aggregate> [--field <field>] [--description <description>] [--filters <json>] [--group-by <groupBy>] [--time-field <timeField>] [--body <json>|--body-file <path>]
  openwop bi metrics update <orgId> <metricId> [--title <title>] [--entity-type <entityType>] [--aggregate <aggregate>] [--field <field>] [--description <description>] [--filters <json>] [--group-by <groupBy>] [--time-field <timeField>] [--body <json>|--body-file <path>]
  openwop bi metrics delete <orgId> <metricId> --yes
  openwop bi metrics run <orgId> <metricId> [--group-by <groupBy>] [--since <since>] [--until <until>] [--bucket <bucket>]

Every write also accepts --body <json> / --body-file <path> for the full request body (typed flags override it).

Endpoints:
  metrics                      GET    /v1/host/openwop-app/bi/orgs/:orgId/metrics
                               Metrics defined in the org (system metrics included).
  metrics get                  GET    /v1/host/openwop-app/bi/orgs/:orgId/metrics/:metricId
                               One metric definition.
  metrics create               POST   /v1/host/openwop-app/bi/orgs/:orgId/metrics
                               Define a metric.
  metrics update               PATCH  /v1/host/openwop-app/bi/orgs/:orgId/metrics/:metricId
                               Edit a metric. The host REPLACES the whole definition, so the CLI reads it first and overlays your flags.
  metrics delete               DELETE /v1/host/openwop-app/bi/orgs/:orgId/metrics/:metricId
                               Delete a stored metric (system metrics refuse).
  metrics run                  POST   /v1/host/openwop-app/bi/orgs/:orgId/metrics/:metricId/run
                               Evaluate a metric now (group by a field, or bucket by day|week|month over a time range).

Business-intelligence metrics (ADR 0417). The host computes every value; the CLI
only relays the definition and prints the host's result points.

Exit codes: 0 ok · 1 server error · 2 usage / not found / validation · 4 not signed in or not permitted.

Examples:
  openwop bi metrics org_1
  openwop bi metrics create org_1 --metric-id open-deals --title "Open deals" --entity-type crm.deal --aggregate count
  openwop bi metrics update org_1 open-deals --group-by stageId
  openwop bi metrics run org_1 open-deals --bucket week --since 2026-07-01T00:00:00Z

Usage:
  openwop capability-firewall rules --org <orgId> [--json]
      GET /v1/host/openwop-app/capability-firewall/orgs/:org/rules — The rule set, unknown-tool policy, mode (default-allow | shadow | enforce) and default-deny verdict.
  openwop capability-firewall rules set --org <orgId> [--rules <json>] [--mode <v>] [--unknown-tool-policy <v>] [--default-deny-verdict <v>] [--body <json> | --body-file <path>] [--json]
      PUT /v1/host/openwop-app/capability-firewall/orgs/:org/rules — Replace settings (org admin). Read-modify-write: fields you do not pass keep their current value; --rules (or --body-file) replaces the whole rule list.
  openwop capability-firewall decisions --org <orgId> [--limit <n>] [--json]
      GET /v1/host/openwop-app/capability-firewall/orgs/:org/decisions — Recent firewall decisions (host default 100, max 500).
  openwop capability-firewall simulate --org <orgId> --next <json> [--seen <json>] [--mode-override <v>] [--context <json>] [--body <json> | --body-file <path>] [--json]
      POST /v1/host/openwop-app/capability-firewall/orgs/:org/simulate — Ask the host what it would decide for a next action after the actions already seen (read-only).
  openwop capability-firewall platform rules [--json]
      GET /v1/host/openwop-app/capability-firewall/platform/rules — The platform baseline rules every tenant inherits (super-admin).
  openwop capability-firewall platform rules set --rules <json> [--body <json> | --body-file <path>] [--json]
      PUT /v1/host/openwop-app/capability-firewall/platform/rules — Replace the platform baseline rules (super-admin).

Capability firewall (host-extension, ADR 0135). A rule is
  {"id","description","when":{"anyOf"|"with"|"countAtLeast"|"expression"},"verdict":"deny"|"require-approval"|"allow","reason"}
and a simulated action is {"toolName":"…"} or a capability class
({"safetyTier":"pure|read|write|exec"}, {"egress":"none|safe-fetch|host-mediated|host-owned"},
{"scope":"…"} or {"kind":"fan-out"}). The rules are tenant-wide even though the path
names an org. The host is the authority: the CLI relays rules and prints the host's
verdicts, never its own.

Flags take the host's field names in kebab-case (priceMinor → --price-minor).
Money amounts are passed through exactly, in the unit the host's field names
(e.g. priceMinor = cents, priceMajorUnits = whole units); the CLI never
computes a price or a total. `--body`/`--body-file` supply the
full JSON body; individual flags override keys in it.

Exit codes: 0 ok · 2 usage error / request rejected · 4 not signed in or not
permitted (HTTP 401/403) · 1 server error.

Examples:
  openwop capability-firewall rules --org org_1
  openwop capability-firewall rules set --org org_1 --mode shadow
  openwop capability-firewall rules set --org org_1 --body-file rules.json
  openwop capability-firewall simulate --org org_1 --next '{"egress":"safe-fetch"}' --seen '[{"safetyTier":"read"}]'
  openwop capability-firewall decisions --org org_1 --limit 20

CMS pages + the authoring lifecycle (host-extension, org-scoped, ADR 0027). A page
moves draft → submit → approve → publish; `versions` lists its history. Every command
needs --org. The host is the authority; the CLI mirrors + relays. `seo` hits the
publishing surface (/v1/host/openwop-app/publishing/…). Writes also accept
--body <json> / --body-file <path> (flags override keys in it).

Exit codes: 0 ok · 2 usage error / request rejected (404, 409, 422) · 4 not signed in
or not permitted (401/403) · 1 server error (incl. 503 translation unavailable).

E-commerce (host-extension /v1/host/openwop-app/commerce/orgs/<orgId>/…, org-scoped;
the public storefront is /v1/host/openwop-app/public-store/<orgId>/… and is
called without credentials). Products, typed product fields, orders (pay /
refund / partial-refund / cancel / fulfillment), the per-user cart, price lists
with a "view as buyer" price preview, quotes, coupons, product subscriptions,
the affiliate ledger, and the revenue summary.

--lines is a JSON array of {"productId":"…","quantity":n} (quotes may add
"unitPrice"). --fulfillment-status is pending | processing | shipped |
delivered; --status on orders list is pending | paid | fulfilled | refunding |
partially_refunded | refunded | canceled; --interval is weekly | monthly |
quarterly | yearly; --commission-type is percentage | fixed. Amounts are passed
through exactly as the host names them — the host computes every total.
--idempotency-key makes an order/checkout create repeat-safe.


UCP (Universal Commerce Protocol). `commerce ucp clients …` manages the
merchant's agent clients (operator auth). The `commerce ucp` agent surface is
PUBLIC: discovery/catalog need no auth; mint a token with

  openwop commerce ucp token --org <orgId> --client-id <id> --client-secret-env <VAR> [--json]
      POST /v1/host/openwop-app/commerce/ucp/orgs/:org/oauth/token — OAuth client_credentials (secret read from the env var, never a flag)

then pass the access token as the global `--api-key` for cart / checkout / order
commands. `ucp order pay` takes `--payment-intent-id` or `--ap2-mandate '{"id":…,"amount":n,"currency":"USD"}'`.
`commerce ucp-buyer …` is the outbound buyer surface (toggle commerce-ucp-buyer);
`purchases close --outcome` is not_placed | confirmed_placed.

Flags take the host's field names in kebab-case (priceMinor → --price-minor).
Money amounts are passed through exactly, in the unit the host's field names
(e.g. priceMinor = cents, priceMajorUnits = whole units); the CLI never
computes a price or a total. `--body`/`--body-file` supply the
full JSON body; individual flags override keys in it.

Exit codes: 0 ok · 2 usage error / request rejected · 4 not signed in or not
permitted (HTTP 401/403) · 1 server error.

Examples:
  openwop commerce products list --org org_1 --q mug
  openwop commerce products create --org org_1 --name Mug --price 12.5 --currency USD --inventory 40
  openwop commerce orders create --org org_1 --lines '[{"productId":"prod_1","quantity":2}]' --idempotency-key ord-42
  openwop commerce orders fulfillment ord_1 --org org_1 --fulfillment-status shipped
  openwop commerce orders partial-refund ord_1 --org org_1 --amount 5 --refund-key adj-1 --yes
  openwop commerce price get --org org_1 --product-id prod_1 --contact-id c_1
  openwop commerce affiliates payouts-csv --org org_1 > payouts.csv
  openwop commerce public products --org org_1 --category mugs
  openwop commerce public checkout --org org_1 --email a@b.co --lines '[{"productId":"prod_1","quantity":1}]'

Usage:
  openwop commerce-connect seller status [--json]

  openwop commerce-connect seller onboard [--country <v>] [--body <json> | --body-file <path>] [--json]

  openwop commerce-connect seller sync [--json]
      POST /v1/host/openwop-app/commerce-connect/seller/sync — Re-read the live seller account state from Stripe.
  openwop commerce-connect seller stats [--json]
      GET /v1/host/openwop-app/commerce-connect/seller/stats — Seller sales stats.
  openwop commerce-connect seller listings [--json]
      GET /v1/host/openwop-app/commerce-connect/seller/listings — List this workspace's own listings (incl. approval state).
  openwop commerce-connect listings list [--json]
      GET /v1/host/openwop-app/commerce-connect/listings — Browse paid listings.
  openwop commerce-connect listings set <packName> --lane <v> [--price-major-units <n>] [--currency <v>] [--external-payment-url <v>] [--body <json> | --body-file <path>] [--json]
      PUT /v1/host/openwop-app/commerce-connect/listings/:packName — Create or update your listing for a pack.
  openwop commerce-connect listings delete <packName> --yes [--json]
      DELETE /v1/host/openwop-app/commerce-connect/listings/:packName — Release your own listing for a pack.
  openwop commerce-connect purchase checkout --pack-name <v> [--body <json> | --body-file <path>] [--json]
      POST /v1/host/openwop-app/commerce-connect/purchase/checkout — Start a purchase of a native-paid listing; returns a Stripe-hosted checkout link.
  openwop commerce-connect orders list [--json]
      GET /v1/host/openwop-app/commerce-connect/orders — List your purchases and sales ({purchases, sales}).
  openwop commerce-connect orders get <orderId> [--json]
      GET /v1/host/openwop-app/commerce-connect/orders/:orderId — Get one order.
  openwop commerce-connect payouts list [--json]
      GET /v1/host/openwop-app/commerce-connect/payouts — List seller payouts.
  openwop commerce-connect approvals list [--json]
      GET /v1/host/openwop-app/commerce-connect/approvals — Superadmin: list pending listing approvals.
  openwop commerce-connect approvals decide <approvalId> --decision <v> [--reason <v>] [--body <json> | --body-file <path>] [--json]
      POST /v1/host/openwop-app/commerce-connect/approvals/:approvalId — Superadmin: approve or reject a listing (a rejection needs --reason).
  openwop commerce-connect admin orders [--json]
      GET /v1/host/openwop-app/commerce-connect/admin/orders — Superadmin: recent orders across sellers.
  openwop commerce-connect admin refund <orderId> --yes [--json]
      POST /v1/host/openwop-app/commerce-connect/admin/orders/:orderId/refund — Superadmin: refund an order.
  openwop commerce-connect admin disputes [--json]
      GET /v1/host/openwop-app/commerce-connect/admin/disputes — Superadmin: disputes + platform loss by currency.
  openwop commerce-connect admin delist <packName> --reason <v> [--body <json> | --body-file <path>] --yes [--json]
      DELETE /v1/host/openwop-app/commerce-connect/admin/listings/:packName — Superadmin: dissolve a listing (tombstone + cooldown).
  openwop commerce-connect admin listing-state <packName> --state <v> --reason <v> [--body <json> | --body-file <path>] [--json]
      PUT /v1/host/openwop-app/commerce-connect/admin/listings/:packName/state — Superadmin: suspend or reactivate a listing.
  openwop commerce-connect import [--sellers <json>] [--body <json> | --body-file <path>] [--json]
      POST /v1/host/openwop-app/commerce-connect/import — Superadmin: import seller account rows ({"sellers":[…]}).
  openwop commerce-connect fee-config get [--tenant-id <v>] [--json]
      GET /v1/host/openwop-app/commerce-connect/fee-config — Superadmin: read the application fee percent (global, or per --tenant-id).
  openwop commerce-connect fee-config set --application-fee-pct <n> [--tenant-id <v>] [--body <json> | --body-file <path>] [--json]
      PUT /v1/host/openwop-app/commerce-connect/fee-config — Superadmin: set the application fee percent (global, or per --tenant-id).

Stripe Connect paid pack listings (host-extension /v1/host/openwop-app/commerce-connect/…).
Sellers onboard through a Stripe-hosted link (`seller onboard` prints it;
open it in a browser), then `seller sync` re-reads the account state. The CLI
never handles card or bank details. --lane is free | external-link |
native-paid; a native-paid listing needs onboarding first and an operator
approval before it is purchasable. `approvals decide` takes --decision
approved | rejected (--reason required on reject). `admin listing-state` takes
--state suspended | active. The approvals / admin / import / fee-config commands
are superadmin-only (HTTP 403 → exit 4 otherwise). Amounts are the host's
major-unit fields, relayed as given.

Flags take the host's field names in kebab-case (priceMinor → --price-minor).
Money amounts are passed through exactly, in the unit the host's field names
(e.g. priceMinor = cents, priceMajorUnits = whole units); the CLI never
computes a price or a total. `--body`/`--body-file` supply the
full JSON body; individual flags override keys in it.

Exit codes: 0 ok · 2 usage error / request rejected · 4 not signed in or not
permitted (HTTP 401/403) · 1 server error.

Examples:
  openwop commerce-connect seller onboard --country US
  openwop commerce-connect listings set my.pack --lane native-paid --price-major-units 19 --currency usd
  openwop commerce-connect purchase checkout --pack-name my.pack
  openwop commerce-connect orders list --json
  openwop commerce-connect approvals decide appr_1 --decision rejected --reason "Pack is missing a README"
  openwop commerce-connect fee-config set --application-fee-pct 10

Usage:
  openwop commissions plans list --org <orgId> [--json]
      GET /v1/host/openwop-app/commissions/orgs/:org/plans — List commission plans.
  openwop commissions plans get <planId> --org <orgId> [--json]
      GET /v1/host/openwop-app/commissions/orgs/:org/plans/:planId — Get one commission plan.
  openwop commissions plans create --org <orgId> --name <v> --currency <v> [--assignment <json>] [--rules <json>] --effective-from <v> [--effective-to <v>] [--body <json> | --body-file <path>] [--json]
      POST /v1/host/openwop-app/commissions/orgs/:org/plans — Create a commission plan.
  openwop commissions plans update <planId> --org <orgId> [--name <v>] [--currency <v>] [--assignment <json>] [--rules <json>] [--effective-from <v>] [--effective-to <v>] [--body <json> | --body-file <path>] [--json]
      PATCH /v1/host/openwop-app/commissions/orgs/:org/plans/:planId — Patch a commission plan.
  openwop commissions plans delete <planId> --org <orgId> --yes [--json]
      DELETE /v1/host/openwop-app/commissions/orgs/:org/plans/:planId — Delete a commission plan (refused once it has approved/paid statements).
  openwop commissions plans compute <planId> --org <orgId> --subject-id <v> --period <v> [--body <json> | --body-file <path>] [--json]
      POST /v1/host/openwop-app/commissions/orgs/:org/plans/:planId/statements/compute — Compute (or recompute) a rep's statement for a period.
  openwop commissions statements list --org <orgId> [--subject-id <v>] [--period <v>] [--plan-id <v>] [--json]
      GET /v1/host/openwop-app/commissions/orgs/:org/statements — List statements (managers see all reps; reps see their own).
  openwop commissions statements get <statementId> --org <orgId> [--json]
      GET /v1/host/openwop-app/commissions/orgs/:org/statements/:statementId — Get one statement.
  openwop commissions statements approve <statementId> --org <orgId> [--json]
      POST /v1/host/openwop-app/commissions/orgs/:org/statements/:statementId/approve — Submit a draft statement for approval (returns the review card).
  openwop commissions statements pay <statementId> --org <orgId> [--json]
      POST /v1/host/openwop-app/commissions/orgs/:org/statements/:statementId/pay — Mark an approved statement paid.

Sales commissions (host-extension /v1/host/openwop-app/commissions/…,
org-scoped). A plan has --currency (ISO-4217, e.g. USD), --effective-from /
--effective-to (YYYY-MM-DD), --assignment {"kind":"territory"|"role"|"rep","ref":"…"}
and --rules [{"basis":"deal-won","type":"percentage"|"fixed","rate":n,
"accelerators":[{"attainmentGte":100,"rate":n}],"cap":n}]. `plans compute`
asks the server to compute a statement for --subject-id over --period;
`statements approve` submits it to the approval gate (decided in the reviews
inbox, exit 0 on 202); `statements pay` records the payout. Totals are the
server's own numbers.

Flags take the host's field names in kebab-case (priceMinor → --price-minor).
Money amounts are passed through exactly, in the unit the host's field names
(e.g. priceMinor = cents, priceMajorUnits = whole units); the CLI never
computes a price or a total. `--body`/`--body-file` supply the
full JSON body; individual flags override keys in it.

Exit codes: 0 ok · 2 usage error / request rejected · 4 not signed in or not
permitted (HTTP 401/403) · 1 server error.

Examples:
  openwop commissions plans list --org org_1
  openwop commissions plans create --org org_1 --name "AE 2026" --currency USD --effective-from 2026-01-01 --assignment '{"kind":"role","ref":"ae"}' --rules '[{"basis":"deal-won","type":"percentage","rate":8}]'
  openwop commissions plans compute plan_1 --org org_1 --subject-id user_7 --period 2026-09
  openwop commissions statements approve stmt_1 --org org_1

Usage:

Every write also accepts --body <json> / --body-file <path> for the full request body (typed flags override it).

Endpoints:
  delete                       DELETE /v1/host/openwop-app/connections/:id
                               Revoke a connection (tears down its inbound binding first). Org connections need connections-manage; user connections, the owner.
  inbound                      GET    /v1/host/openwop-app/connections/:id/inbound
                               The connection's inbound webhook binding + the ingest URL to give the provider.
  inbound set                  PUT    /v1/host/openwop-app/connections/:id/inbound
                               Bind inbound events to a workflow (slack, discord, telegram, whatsapp, zoom-webinar, stream). The signing secret is read from a file, never from the command line.
  inbound remove               DELETE /v1/host/openwop-app/connections/:id/inbound
                               Remove the inbound binding.
  providers                    GET    /v1/host/openwop-app/providers | /v1/host/openwop-app/providers/:id
                               The connection-provider catalog (or one provider's manifest): auth flow, scopes, whether OAuth is configured here.


Inspect the host's third-party connections and their OAuth client configuration
(ADR 0024). `list`/`get` render connection metadata + status; `test` health-probes
one credential (the host refreshes OAuth on the way); `authorize` mints a consent
URL for a provider — it returns the URL only, the CLI never completes the OAuth
exchange. `oauth-clients` shows the host-configured OAuth apps (superadmin).

SECRET BOUNDARY: client secrets and tokens are host-side and are NEVER returned,
printed, or logged — only refs and status. The CLI additionally redacts any
secret-looking field defensively before printing.

The host is the authority — the CLI renders its resolved view and fails closed if
the connections surface isn't advertised (/.well-known/openwop).

Endpoints:
  list           GET  /v1/host/openwop-app/connections
  get            GET  /v1/host/openwop-app/connections  (filtered to <id> client-side;
                 the host exposes no single-connection GET)

  authorize      POST /v1/host/openwop-app/connections/{provider}/authorize
  oauth-clients  GET  /v1/host/openwop-app/connections-oauth-clients[/{provider} filtered]

  --scope <s>     (authorize) An OAuth scope to request (repeatable).
  --write         (authorize) Request write scopes (re-consent for write access).
  --return-to <u> (authorize) Where the host should bounce the browser back to.
  --json          Print the (redacted) raw host response instead of the table.

Exit codes:
  list/get/authorize/oauth-clients  0 ok · 2 usage · 1 not-found/error
  test                              0 connection healthy · 1 unhealthy/error

  openwop connections get conn:abc --json
  openwop connections test conn:abc
  openwop connections authorize google --scope https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar --write
  openwop connections oauth-clients list

Usage:
  openwop consent policy <orgId> [--json]
  openwop consent set-policy <orgId> [--default-mode opt-in|opt-out] [--regulated-region <r>]... [--json]
  openwop consent records <orgId> [--json]
  openwop consent get <orgId> <subjectKey> [--json]
  openwop consent erase <orgId> <subjectKey> [--yes] [--json]
  openwop consent public get <orgId> <subjectKey> [--json]
  openwop consent public record <orgId> <subjectKey> [--category <name=bool>]... [--region <r>] [--json]
  openwop consent purposes <orgId> [--json]
  openwop consent purposes add <orgId> --code <code>
  openwop consent purposes remove <orgId> <code> --yes
  openwop consent purposes strict <orgId> --strict
  openwop consent readmit <orgId> <subjectKey> [--attestation <attestation>] --yes

Every write also accepts --body <json> / --body-file <path> for the full request body (typed flags override it).

Endpoints:
  purposes                     GET    /v1/host/openwop-app/consent/orgs/:orgId/purpose-vocab
                               The tenant's known purpose codes + whether capture is strict.
  purposes add                 POST   /v1/host/openwop-app/consent/orgs/:orgId/purpose-vocab
                               Register a purpose code.
  purposes remove              DELETE /v1/host/openwop-app/consent/orgs/:orgId/purpose-vocab/:code
                               Remove a purpose code.
  purposes strict              PUT    /v1/host/openwop-app/consent/orgs/:orgId/purpose-vocab/strict
                               Refuse (--strict) or accept (--no-strict) unknown purpose codes at capture.
  readmit                      POST   /v1/host/openwop-app/consent/orgs/:orgId/subjects/:subjectKey/readmit
                               Clear an erased subject's tombstone so they can opt in again (grants nothing; admin).

Tenant-scoped consent (ADR 0020). The host is the authority: consent is stored
per-tenant and the host resolves a subject's effective categories. This command
RENDERS the host's resolved view — it never computes or asserts a consent outcome
locally. The org→tenant mapping and the per-tenant 'consent' feature toggle are
enforced host-side; when the toggle is off the host returns a uniform 404 and this
command fails closed with a legible message (it does not assume permissive).

Authed, org-scoped (RBAC) — hits /v1/host/openwop-app/consent/orgs/<orgId>/*:
  policy        GET  .../policy        Show the tenant consent policy (defaultMode + regulated regions).
  set-policy    PUT  .../policy        Update defaultMode and/or regulatedRegions (workspace:write).
  records       GET  .../records       List all consent records for the tenant.
  get           GET  .../subjects/<k>  Show one subject's consent record (or none).
  erase         DEL  .../subjects/<k>  GDPR erasure — purge the record + fan out to feature erasers (idempotent).

Public, unauthed — hits /v1/host/openwop-app/public-consent/<orgId>:
  public get    GET  .../<k>           Read a visitor's recorded categories, or the policy default if none.
  public record POST .../             Record a visitor's category choices (source=public).

  --default-mode <m>      (set-policy) opt-in | opt-out.
  --regulated-region <r>  (set-policy) A regulated region code (repeatable; replaces the list).
  --category <name=bool>  (public record) A category choice, e.g. analytics=true (repeatable).
  --region <r>            (public record) The visitor's region.
  --yes                   (erase) Confirm the destructive GDPR erasure.

Exit codes: 0 success · 1 host/HTTP error (incl. consent not enabled) · 2 usage error.

Examples:
  openwop consent policy org_123
  openwop consent set-policy org_123 --default-mode opt-out --regulated-region EU --regulated-region UK
  openwop consent records org_123 --json
  openwop consent get org_123 visitor-abc
  openwop consent erase org_123 visitor-abc --yes
  openwop consent public get org_123 visitor-abc
  openwop consent public record org_123 visitor-abc --category analytics=true --category marketing=false

CRM extensions (host-extension /v1/host/openwop-app/crm/*). Tenant-wide: contact scoring,
conversion, merge (+ steward merge proposals and reversible unmerge),
identifiers, duplicate review, CSV export, contact custom fields, saved segments
(--filters is the host's filter JSON array), the do-not-contact suppression list
(--reason unsubscribed|bounced|complaint|manual), and Gmail activity sync (the
connection must be your own; the host refuses anyone else's).

Org-scoped CRM (host-extension /v1/host/openwop-app/crm/orgs/<orgId>/…, pass
--org): pipelines, companies (+ merge/unmerge, duplicates with
--entity-type company), deals (+ stage history, pipeline report), tasks
(status open|doing|done), activities (kind note|call|email|meeting|webinar; the activity's `body` field
is given as --text, since --body is the whole-JSON-body flag),
org custom fields (entity company|deal; type string|number|boolean|date|enum|reference),
JSON import (--rows '[{…}]', or the whole body via --body-file) and CSV export
(--entity-type companies|deals|tasks|activities). Deal --amount is passed
through exactly as the host stores it.

Booking links + e-signature (ADR 0402). `public-book` and `public-sign` are
the visitor surfaces (/v1/host/openwop-app/public-book|public-sign/…) and are
sent without your API key: a published link's slug, or the capability token
from a manage/signer link. --target is {"kind":"<kind>","id":"<id>"};
--signers is [{"email":"…","name":"…","order":1}]. Signing requires
--acknowledged true (the legal notice) and --typed-name.

Examples:
  openwop crm deals list --org org_1 --pipeline-id p1
  openwop crm deals update deal_1 --org org_1 --stage-id won
  openwop crm org-export --org org_1 --entity-type deals > deals.csv
  openwop crm public-book slots my-demo --duration-min 30 --from 1790000000000 --to 1790600000000
  openwop crm public-sign sign <token> --acknowledged true --typed-name "Ada Lovelace"

Flags take the host's field names in kebab-case (priceMinor → --price-minor).
Money amounts are passed through exactly, in the unit the host's field names
(e.g. priceMinor = cents, priceMajorUnits = whole units); the CLI never
computes a price or a total. `--body`/`--body-file` supply the
full JSON body; individual flags override keys in it.

                               Which conversation the AI briefing tile shows.
  briefing set                 PUT    /v1/host/openwop-app/dashboard/briefing
                               Point the briefing tile at a conversation.

Personal dashboard state (ADR 0375 / 0577). Everything is yours alone — no org.

      POST /v1/host/openwop-app/dealers/orgs/:org/dealers — Create a dealer (references a CRM company).
  openwop dealers update <dealerId> --org <orgId> [--name <v>] [--tier <v>] [--status <v>] [--territory-id <v>] [--body <json> | --body-file <path>] [--json]

  openwop dealers delete <dealerId> --org <orgId> --yes [--json]

  openwop dealers portal-token <dealerId> --org <orgId> [--json]
      POST /v1/host/openwop-app/dealers/orgs/:org/dealers/:dealerId/portal-token — Mint/rotate the dealer's partner-portal link.
  openwop dealers outlets list --org <orgId> [--dealer-id <v>] [--json]
      GET /v1/host/openwop-app/dealers/orgs/:org/outlets — List outlets (optionally one dealer's).
  openwop dealers outlets for-dealer <dealerId> --org <orgId> [--json]
      GET /v1/host/openwop-app/dealers/orgs/:org/dealers/:dealerId/outlets — List one dealer's outlets (404 if the dealer is unknown).
  openwop dealers outlets get <outletId> --org <orgId> [--json]
      GET /v1/host/openwop-app/dealers/orgs/:org/outlets/:outletId — Get one outlet.
  openwop dealers outlets create <dealerId> --org <orgId> --name <v> [--status <v>] [--address <v>] [--lat <n>] [--lng <n>] [--body <json> | --body-file <path>] [--json]
      POST /v1/host/openwop-app/dealers/orgs/:org/dealers/:dealerId/outlets — Create an outlet under a dealer.
  openwop dealers outlets update <outletId> --org <orgId> [--name <v>] [--status <v>] [--address <v>] [--lat <n>] [--lng <n>] [--body <json> | --body-file <path>] [--json]

  openwop dealers outlets delete <outletId> --org <orgId> --yes [--json]
      DELETE /v1/host/openwop-app/dealers/orgs/:org/outlets/:outletId — Delete an outlet.
  openwop dealers registrations --org <orgId> [--dealer-id <v>] [--status <v>] [--json]
      GET /v1/host/openwop-app/dealers/orgs/:org/registrations — List deal registrations (decide them in the reviews inbox).
  openwop dealers partner get <token> [--json]
      GET /v1/host/openwop-app/partner/:token  (public, no auth) — Read the partner-portal view for a portal token.
  openwop dealers partner register <token> --deal-title <v> --company-name <v> [--body <json> | --body-file <path>] [--json]
      POST /v1/host/openwop-app/partner/:token/register  (public, no auth) — Register a deal through the partner portal.

Dealer network (host-extension /v1/host/openwop-app/dealers/…, org-scoped). A
dealer references a CRM company (--company-id); --status is active | suspended
for dealers and active | closed for outlets. `portal-token` mints the dealer's
partner-portal link (a bearer credential, shown once). `partner get|register`
drive the PUBLIC portal (/v1/host/openwop-app/partner/<token>, no auth) exactly
as a dealer would. Registrations are approved/rejected in the reviews inbox.

Flags take the host's field names in kebab-case (priceMinor → --price-minor).
Money amounts are passed through exactly, in the unit the host's field names
(e.g. priceMinor = cents, priceMajorUnits = whole units); the CLI never
computes a price or a total. `--body`/`--body-file` supply the
full JSON body; individual flags override keys in it.

Exit codes: 0 ok · 2 usage error / request rejected · 4 not signed in or not
permitted (HTTP 401/403) · 1 server error.

Examples:
  openwop dealers list --org org_1 --status active
  openwop dealers create --org org_1 --company-id company:abc --name "Acme Motors" --tier gold
  openwop dealers outlets create dealer:123 --org org_1 --name "Downtown" --lat 40.7 --lng=-74.0
  openwop dealers portal-token dealer:123 --org org_1
  openwop dealers partner register <token> --deal-title "Fleet renewal" --company-name "Globex"

help.stdout:
Usage:
  openwop goals list [--state <s>] [--json]
  openwop goals get <goalId> [--json]
  openwop goals create --objective <text> [--judge host|verifier] [--continuation <mode>]
                       [--max-iterations <n>] [--max-cost <usd>] [--timeout-ms <ms>] [--json]
  openwop goals pause <goalId> [--json]
  openwop goals resume <goalId> [--json]
  openwop goals abandon <goalId> [--yes]
  openwop goals arm <id> --workflow-id <workflowId> --cron-expr <cronExpr> [--timezone <timezone>]
  openwop goals evaluate <id> --snapshot-ref <snapshotRef> --snapshot-hash <snapshotHash>
  openwop goals record-run <id> --run-id <runId> [--cost-usd <costUsd>]

Every write also accepts --body <json> / --body-file <path> for the full request body (typed flags override it).

Endpoints:
  arm                          POST   /v1/host/openwop-app/goals/:id/arm
                               Arm a schedule continuation: run --workflow-id on --cron-expr until the judge is satisfied or a bound stops it.
  evaluate                     POST   /v1/host/openwop-app/goals/:id/evaluate
                               Ask the host judge to verdict a snapshot (the host decides; replay-safe by snapshot hash).
  record-run                   POST   /v1/host/openwop-app/goals/:id/runs
                               Attribute a run (and its cost) to the goal's progress + bounds.


Standing goals (RFC 0097). A goal is an objective the host pursues across runs
until a JUDGE (RFC 0090) verdicts it satisfied or a BOUND (RFC 0058) stops it.
'list'/'get' render the host's goals. 'create' opens a goal with its judge,
continuation arm(s), and bounds. 'pause'/'resume' suspend/restart continuation;
'abandon' closes the goal.

Completion is the host judge's verdict — there is no `complete`/`satisfy` verb
and the CLI never sets satisfied; you cannot declare victory from the client. The
host is the authority; the CLI renders its resolved view and relays your verb. If
the host does not advertise the goal surface (/.well-known/openwop), the group
fails closed rather than guessing.

Endpoints:
  list     GET    /v1/host/openwop-app/goals[?state=]
  get      GET    /v1/host/openwop-app/goals/{id}
  create   POST   /v1/host/openwop-app/goals          (422 if the host requires bounds and none given)
  pause    POST   /v1/host/openwop-app/goals/{id}/pause
  resume   POST   /v1/host/openwop-app/goals/{id}/resume
  abandon  POST   /v1/host/openwop-app/goals/{id}/abandon

  --state <s>            (list) Filter by state (e.g. active, satisfied, escalated, bound-exceeded, paused).
  --objective <text>     (create) The goal objective (required).
  --judge host|verifier  (create) completion.check — who decides completion (default: host).
  --continuation <mode>  (create) continuation.mode — the arm that re-engages work (e.g. schedule | commitment | manual).
  --max-iterations <n>   (create) Bound: bounds.maxLoopIterations.
  --max-cost <usd>       (create) Bound: bounds.maxCostUsd (accumulated USD).
  --timeout-ms <ms>      (create) Bound: bounds.runTimeoutMs (wall-clock, milliseconds).
  --yes                  (abandon) Required to confirm.
  --json                 Print the raw host response instead of the rendered view.

Boundary: a goal is NOT an RFC 0068 commitment — a goal *uses* a

termination guarantee (bounds).

] [--json] openwop kanban card-move --column [--json] openwop kanban card-update [--title ] [--description ] [--column ] [--workflow ] [--json] openwop kanban card-delete [--yes] openwop kanban card-assign --assignee [--role ] [--no-notify] [--json] openwop kanban card-claim [--json] openwop kanban boards-personal [--json] openwop kanban assigned [--json] openwop kanban watch Kanban boards (host-extension under /v1/host/openwop-app/kanban). A board is a lane of cards an agent works; a board MAY bind to an RFC 0086 roster entry so its To Do column fires the named agent's first portfolio workflow. 'watch' streams the board's server-sent card events until interrupted. --column (board-create) A column, repeatable; default lanes if omitted. --trigger-workflow (board-create) Workflow the To Do column fires. --roster (board-create) Bind the board to a roster entry (RFC 0086). --priority

(card-add) low | normal | high | urgent. Examples: openwop kanban boards openwop kanban board-create --name "Sally's work" --roster r_123 openwop kanban card-add b_1 --title "Triage inbox" --column todo openwop kanban card-move c_9 --column working openwop kanban watch b_1 openwop kanban column-limit --wip-limit openwop kanban column-limit clear openwop kanban work-item-run Every write also accepts --body / --body-file for the full request body (typed flags override it). Usage:

  openwop operations slo [--json]
  openwop operations dlq [--tenant-id <tenantId>] [--json]
  openwop operations dlq replay --tenant-id <tenantId> --subject <subject> --message-id <messageId>
  openwop operations outbox [--json]
  openwop operations outbox redrive <runId> --reason <reason>
  openwop operations webhooks [<orgId>] [--tenant-id <tenantId>] [--json]
  openwop operations webhooks retry <deliveryId>
  openwop operations triggers set-state <subscriptionId> --state <state>
  openwop operations compensation <runId> [--json]
  openwop operations compensation act <runId> --action <action> --obligation-id <obligationId> --expected-state <expectedState> [--reason <reason>] [--node-type-id <nodeTypeId>]

Every write also accepts --body <json> / --body-file <path> for the full request body (typed flags override it).

Endpoints:
  health                       GET    /v1/host/openwop-app/operations/health/summary
                               Host health rollup (providers, config, storage, SSE, rate limits, daemon). Superadmin.
  slo                          GET    /v1/host/openwop-app/operations/slo/summary
                               SLO rows + active alerts from the local metrics scrape. Superadmin.
  dlq                          GET    /v1/host/openwop-app/operations/dlq/summary
                               Dead-letter queue depth per subject. Superadmin.
  dlq replay                   POST   /v1/host/openwop-app/operations/dlq/replay
                               Replay one dead-lettered message (202). Superadmin.
  outbox                       GET    /v1/host/openwop-app/operations/dispatch-outbox/summary
                               Run-dispatch outbox: pending/dead counts + dead rows. Superadmin.
  outbox redrive               POST   /v1/host/openwop-app/operations/dispatch-outbox/:runId/redrive
                               Re-drive a dead outbox row (202). Superadmin; the reason is audit-logged.
  webhooks                     GET    /v1/host/openwop-app/operations/webhooks/summary | /v1/host/openwop-app/operations/orgs/:orgId/webhooks/summary
                               Webhook + trigger-subscription delivery health. No <orgId> = all tenants (superadmin, optional --tenant-id); with <orgId> = your tenant (webhooks:manage).
  webhooks retry               POST   /v1/host/openwop-app/operations/webhooks/deliveries/:deliveryId/retry
                               Retry one failed webhook delivery (202). Superadmin.
  triggers set-state           POST   /v1/host/openwop-app/operations/trigger-subscriptions/:subscriptionId/state
                               Pause or resume a trigger subscription. Superadmin.
  compensation                 GET    /v1/host/openwop-app/operations/runs/:runId/compensation
                               A run's compensation status + obligations (host:compensation:start).
  compensation act             POST   /v1/host/openwop-app/operations/runs/:runId/compensation/actions
                               Apply a recovery action to one obligation: start | retry | skip | substitute | terminate (409 approval_required when a second approver is needed).

Operator console (ADR 0395). Summaries are point-in-time reads; several are per
server instance (the body says `perInstance`). Recovery verbs are audit-logged by the
host. The host decides every action — a refused one comes back as its error.

Exit codes: 0 ok · 1 server error (or 5xx) · 2 usage / not found / validation · 4 not signed in or not permitted (most summaries need a super-admin).

Examples:
  openwop operations health --json
  openwop operations dlq --tenant-id t_1
  openwop operations dlq replay --tenant-id t_1 --subject runs.dispatch.dlq --message-id m_9
  openwop operations outbox redrive run_42 --reason "provider outage cleared"
  openwop operations webhooks org_123
  openwop operations compensation run_42
  openwop operations compensation act run_42 --action retry --obligation-id ob_1 --expected-state failed

  openwop priority-matrix ideas schedule clear <listId> <cardId> --yes
  openwop priority-matrix schedule <listId> [--json]
  openwop priority-matrix sessions <listId> [--json]
  openwop priority-matrix sessions create <listId> [--name <name>] [--mode <mode>] [--n <n>] [--card-ids <cardIds>] [--sort <sort>] [--sort-dir <sortDir>] [--rationale <rationale>]
  openwop priority-matrix sessions update <listId> <sessionId> [--sort <sort>] [--sort-dir <sortDir>] [--rationale <rationale>]
  openwop priority-matrix scenarios <listId> <sessionId> [--json]
  openwop priority-matrix scenarios create <listId> <sessionId> --name <name> [--mode <mode>] [--n <n>] [--card-ids <cardIds>] [--max-items <maxItems>] [--max-budget <maxBudget>]
  openwop priority-matrix scenarios compare <listId> <sessionId> --a <a> --b <b> [--json]
  openwop priority-matrix scenarios select <listId> <sessionId> <scenarioId>

Every write also accepts --body <json> / --body-file <path> for the full request body (typed flags override it).

Endpoints:
  update                       PATCH  /v1/host/openwop-app/priority-matrix/lists/:listId
                               Merge-patch a list. Criteria / voting changes need list-config authority (creator or org manager).
  ideas                        GET    /v1/host/openwop-app/priority-matrix/lists/:listId/ideas
                               Ranked ideas in a list.
  ideas add                    POST   /v1/host/openwop-app/priority-matrix/lists/:listId/ideas
                               Add an idea (lands in the "new" column).
  ideas update                 PATCH  /v1/host/openwop-app/priority-matrix/lists/:listId/ideas/:cardId
                               Edit an idea's title / description ("" clears the description).
  ideas delete                 DELETE /v1/host/openwop-app/priority-matrix/lists/:listId/ideas/:cardId
                               Delete an idea.
  ideas clone                  POST   /v1/host/openwop-app/priority-matrix/lists/:listId/ideas/:cardId/clone
                               Clone an idea (title defaults to "<title> (copy)").
  ideas merge                  POST   /v1/host/openwop-app/priority-matrix/lists/:listId/ideas/:cardId/merge
                               Merge a duplicate into this (canonical) idea; the duplicate is cancelled.
  ideas promote                POST   /v1/host/openwop-app/priority-matrix/lists/:listId/ideas/:cardId/promote-to-project
                               Promote an idea to a new project (moves the card to done).
  ideas status                 PATCH  /v1/host/openwop-app/priority-matrix/lists/:listId/ideas/:cardId/status
                               Move an idea to a board column.
  ideas score                  PUT    /v1/host/openwop-app/priority-matrix/lists/:listId/ideas/:cardId/scores
                               Score an idea. REPLACES the scores: criteria you omit are cleared (multi-voter lists write your own vote).
  ideas score-history          GET    /v1/host/openwop-app/priority-matrix/lists/:listId/ideas/:cardId/score-history
                               Score changes + the per-criterion breakdown.
  ideas votes                  GET    /v1/host/openwop-app/priority-matrix/lists/:listId/ideas/:cardId/votes
                               Per-voter scores on a multi-voter list (list-config authority).
  ideas intake                 GET    /v1/host/openwop-app/priority-matrix/lists/:listId/ideas/:cardId/intake
                               Intake details + evidence links for an idea.
  ideas intake set             PATCH  /v1/host/openwop-app/priority-matrix/lists/:listId/ideas/:cardId/intake
                               Merge-patch intake details ("" clears a text field).
  ideas evidence add           POST   /v1/host/openwop-app/priority-matrix/lists/:listId/ideas/:cardId/evidence
                               Link evidence (document | kb | url) to an idea.
  ideas evidence remove        DELETE /v1/host/openwop-app/priority-matrix/lists/:listId/ideas/:cardId/evidence/:evidenceId
                               Remove an evidence link.
  ideas schedule set           PUT    /v1/host/openwop-app/priority-matrix/lists/:listId/ideas/:cardId/schedule
                               Set an idea's target (and optional start) date — replaces the schedule.
  ideas schedule clear         DELETE /v1/host/openwop-app/priority-matrix/lists/:listId/ideas/:cardId/schedule
                               Clear an idea's schedule.
  schedule                     GET    /v1/host/openwop-app/priority-matrix/lists/:listId/schedule
                               Delivery schedule for every idea + a rollup (on-track / at-risk / behind ...).
  sessions                     GET    /v1/host/openwop-app/priority-matrix/lists/:listId/sessions
                               Planning sessions for a list.
  sessions create              POST   /v1/host/openwop-app/priority-matrix/lists/:listId/sessions
                               Start a planning session (top-n | manual | both selection; writes an agenda document when documents is on).
  sessions update              PATCH  /v1/host/openwop-app/priority-matrix/lists/:listId/sessions/:sessionId
                               Re-sort a session's agenda or edit its rationale.
  scenarios                    GET    /v1/host/openwop-app/priority-matrix/lists/:listId/sessions/:sessionId/scenarios
                               What-if scenarios in a session (above / below the line).
  scenarios create             POST   /v1/host/openwop-app/priority-matrix/lists/:listId/sessions/:sessionId/scenarios
                               Add a scenario: --mode top-n --n <k>, or --mode manual --card-ids a,b; optional --max-items / --max-budget.
  scenarios compare            GET    /v1/host/openwop-app/priority-matrix/lists/:listId/sessions/:sessionId/scenarios/compare
                               Diff two scenarios (what B gains / drops vs A).
  scenarios select             POST   /v1/host/openwop-app/priority-matrix/lists/:listId/sessions/:sessionId/scenarios/:scenarioId/select
                               Make a scenario the plan of record (an agent-proposed one is decided through its approval).
  scenarios reject             POST   /v1/host/openwop-app/priority-matrix/lists/:listId/sessions/:sessionId/scenarios/:scenarioId/reject
                               Reject an agent-proposed scenario.
  portfolio                    GET    /v1/host/openwop-app/priority-matrix/portfolio
                               Top ideas across every list you can read.
  portfolio federated          GET    /v1/host/openwop-app/priority-matrix/portfolio/federated
                               Portfolio merged with every federated peer host (each peer fails soft).
  presets                      GET    /v1/host/openwop-app/priority-matrix/presets
                               Built-in scoring presets (weighted, WSJF, RICE, ICE, value-effort).
  peers                        GET    /v1/host/openwop-app/priority-matrix/peers
                               Federated peer hosts.
  peers add                    POST   /v1/host/openwop-app/priority-matrix/peers
                               Add a federated peer (https only; superadmin).
  peers remove                 DELETE /v1/host/openwop-app/priority-matrix/peers/:peerId
                               Remove a peer and its shared credential (superadmin).
  peers credential             PUT    /v1/host/openwop-app/priority-matrix/peers/:peerId/credential
                               Store the bearer for a peer (sealed host-side, never echoed). Read from a file so it never lands in shell history. --scope tenant (superadmin) | user.
  reindex-kb                   POST   /v1/host/openwop-app/priority-matrix/reindex-kb
                               Re-index an org's priority lists into the knowledge base.

Prioritization boards (host-extension). A list holds scored/voted ideas; `ideas` reads
a list's ideas. `create` needs the owning --org. The host is the authority.

Usage:
  openwop profiles list [--json]
  openwop profiles get [<userId>] [--json]            (omit userId for your own — same as 'me')
  openwop profiles me [--json]
  openwop profiles activity [--limit <n>] [--status <s>] [--json]
  openwop profiles edit [--preferred-name <t>] [--job-title <t>] [--department <t>] [--bio <t>] [--location <t>]
                        [--link <label=url>]... [--equipment <x>]... [--interests <x>]... [--growth-interests <x>]...
                        [--availability-status available|busy|away] [--timezone <tz>] [--hours-per-week <n>] [--json]
  openwop profiles skills set --skill <name=proficiency>... [--json]
  openwop profiles portfolio add --token <mediaToken> [--json]
  openwop profiles portfolio remove <mediaToken> [--json]
  openwop profiles pin <rosterId> [--json]
  openwop profiles unpin <rosterId> [--json]
  openwop profiles endorse <userId> <skill> [--json]
  openwop profiles unendorse <userId> <skill> [--json]
  openwop profiles pin-chat <rosterId>
  openwop profiles unpin-chat <rosterId>
  openwop profiles avatar set --token <token>
  openwop profiles avatar clear
  openwop profiles workflows set --workflows <workflows>
  openwop profiles knowledge bind --collection-id <collectionId>
  openwop profiles knowledge unbind <collectionId> --yes
  openwop profiles knowledge collections create --org <orgId> --name <name> [--description <description>]
  openwop profiles knowledge documents add <collectionId> --org <orgId> [--title <title>] [--text <text>] [--text-file <path>] [--media-token <mediaToken>]
  openwop profiles knowledge documents remove <collectionId> <documentId> --org <orgId> --yes
  openwop profiles knowledge retrieve --query <query>
  openwop profiles memory remove <noteId> --yes
  openwop profiles memory-extraction [--json]
  openwop profiles memory-extraction grant
  openwop profiles memory-extraction revoke

Every write also accepts --body <json> / --body-file <path> for the full request body (typed flags override it).

Endpoints:
  pin-chat                     PUT    /v1/host/openwop-app/profiles/me/pinned-chat-agents/:rosterId
                               Pin an agent to your AI-chat welcome screen.
  unpin-chat                   DELETE /v1/host/openwop-app/profiles/me/pinned-chat-agents/:rosterId
                               Unpin an agent from your AI-chat welcome screen.
  avatar set                   PUT    /v1/host/openwop-app/profiles/me/avatar
                               Set your avatar from a tenant image media token.
  avatar clear                 DELETE /v1/host/openwop-app/profiles/me/avatar
                               Remove your avatar.
  workflows set                PUT    /v1/host/openwop-app/profiles/me/workflows
                               REPLACE the workflows on your profile.
  knowledge bind               POST   /v1/host/openwop-app/profiles/me/knowledge/bindings
                               Bind a knowledge collection to your profile.
  knowledge unbind             DELETE /v1/host/openwop-app/profiles/me/knowledge/bindings/:collectionId
                               Unbind a collection from your profile.
  knowledge collections create POST   /v1/host/openwop-app/profiles/me/knowledge/collections
                               Create a collection in --org and bind it to your profile.
  knowledge documents add      POST   /v1/host/openwop-app/profiles/me/knowledge/collections/:collectionId/documents
                               Add a document: inline --text, a --text-file, or an uploaded --media-token.
  knowledge documents remove   DELETE /v1/host/openwop-app/profiles/me/knowledge/collections/:collectionId/documents/:documentId
                               Remove a document (the host needs its --org).
  knowledge retrieve           POST   /v1/host/openwop-app/profiles/me/knowledge/retrieve
                               Retrieve chunks from your personal knowledge + memory.
  memory remove                DELETE /v1/host/openwop-app/profiles/me/memory/:noteId
                               Forget one of your memory notes.
  memory-extraction            GET    /v1/host/openwop-app/profiles/me/memory-extraction
                               Whether you have granted automatic memory extraction from your chats.
  memory-extraction grant      PUT    /v1/host/openwop-app/profiles/me/memory-extraction
                               Grant automatic memory extraction (your own consent; nobody else can grant it).
  memory-extraction revoke     DELETE /v1/host/openwop-app/profiles/me/memory-extraction
                               Revoke the grant (extraction stops; existing notes stay until you remove them).


Self-service PERSONA: your job title, bio, contact, skills, availability, portfolio,
and pinned agents (ADR 0005). The host is the authority and renders the resolved view —
reads are visible to any signed-in tenant member; writes only ever touch YOUR OWN profile
(authority is intrinsic to the caller's resolved identity). Tenant-scoped throughout; a
foreign-tenant id reads as 404. Requires a durable signed-in account (bearer via --api-key).

BOUNDARY: `profiles` is the persona/skills surface, NOT the user directory (account
lifecycle lives in the host's users surface) and NOT RBAC (that's `orgs`). `profiles list`
is the persona directory of the tenant, not an account-management list.

  --job-title/--department/--bio/--location   (edit) Text fields; pass empty string to clear.
  --equipment/--interests/--growth-interests <x>  (edit) Repeatable; replaces the whole list.
  --link <label=url>                          (edit) Repeatable contact link; replaces the link list (location is kept).
  --availability-status / --timezone / --hours-per-week  (edit) Availability sub-fields.
  --skill <name=proficiency>                  (skills set) Repeatable; proficiency is 1..5. Replaces the skill list.
  --token <mediaToken>                        (portfolio add) A tenant media-asset token (must be an image).
  --limit <n> / --status <s>                  (activity) Page size (1..50) / run-status filter.

Exit codes: 0 success · 1 host/HTTP error (incl. not found / not signed in) · 2 usage error.

Examples:
  openwop profiles me
  openwop profiles get user_42 --json
  openwop profiles edit --job-title "Staff Engineer" --availability-status busy --timezone Europe/London
  openwop profiles skills set --skill TypeScript=5 --skill Rust=3
  openwop profiles endorse user_42 TypeScript
  openwop profiles pin r_123
  openwop profiles activity --limit 10 --status failed

help.stdout:
Usage:
  openwop projects list [--json]
  openwop projects get <projectId> [--json]
  openwop projects create --org <orgId> --name <n> [--json]
  openwop projects delete <projectId> [--yes]
  openwop projects members list <projectId> [--json]
  openwop projects members remove <projectId> <ref> [--yes]
  openwop projects update <id> [--name <name>] [--workflows <workflows>] [--charter <json>] [--moderator-roster-id <moderatorRosterId>] [--turn-policy <json>] [--body <json>|--body-file <path>]
  openwop projects visibility <id> --visibility <visibility>
  openwop projects members add <id> --ref <ref> [--role <role>]
  openwop projects knowledge <id> [--json]
  openwop projects knowledge bind <id> --collection-id <collectionId>
  openwop projects knowledge unbind <id> <collectionId> --yes
  openwop projects knowledge collections create <id> --org <orgId> --name <name> [--description <description>]
  openwop projects knowledge documents add <id> <collectionId> --org <orgId> [--title <title>] [--text <text>] [--text-file <path>] [--file <path>] [--content-type <contentType>]
  openwop projects knowledge documents remove <id> <collectionId> <documentId> --org <orgId> --yes
  openwop projects knowledge retrieve <id> --query <query>
  openwop projects memory <id> [--json]
  openwop projects memory add <id> --content <content>
  openwop projects memory remove <id> <noteId> --yes
  openwop projects schedules <id> [--json]
  openwop projects schedules add <id> --cron-expr <cronExpr> [--workflow-id <workflowId>] [--timezone <timezone>]
  openwop projects schedules update <id> <jobId> [--enabled] [--cron-expr <cronExpr>] [--workflow-id <workflowId>] [--timezone <timezone>]
  openwop projects schedules remove <id> <jobId> --yes
  openwop projects chat <id>

Every write also accepts --body <json> / --body-file <path> for the full request body (typed flags override it).

Endpoints:
  update                       PATCH  /v1/host/openwop-app/projects/:id
                               Merge-patch a project. --workflows and --charter REPLACE their whole value (charter null clears).
  visibility                   PATCH  /v1/host/openwop-app/projects/:id/visibility
                               Set who can see a project: org | private.
  members add                  POST   /v1/host/openwop-app/projects/:id/members
                               Add (or re-role) a member: user:<userId> | agent:<rosterId>; role lead | contributor | observer.
  knowledge                    GET    /v1/host/openwop-app/projects/:id/knowledge
                               Knowledge bound to the project (collections, documents, note count).
  knowledge bind               POST   /v1/host/openwop-app/projects/:id/knowledge/bindings
                               Bind an existing knowledge collection to the project.
  knowledge unbind             DELETE /v1/host/openwop-app/projects/:id/knowledge/bindings/:collectionId
                               Unbind a collection (the collection itself is kept).
  knowledge collections create POST   /v1/host/openwop-app/projects/:id/knowledge/collections
                               Create a collection in --org and bind it to the project.
  knowledge documents add      POST   /v1/host/openwop-app/projects/:id/knowledge/collections/:collectionId/documents
                               Add a document to a bound collection: inline --text, a text file, or a binary --file (sent base64 inside the JSON body).
  knowledge documents remove   DELETE /v1/host/openwop-app/projects/:id/knowledge/collections/:collectionId/documents/:documentId
                               Remove a document (the host needs its --org in the body).
  knowledge retrieve           POST   /v1/host/openwop-app/projects/:id/knowledge/retrieve
                               Retrieve chunks from the project's knowledge + memory for a query.
  memory                       GET    /v1/host/openwop-app/projects/:id/memory
                               Project memory notes.
  memory add                   POST   /v1/host/openwop-app/projects/:id/memory
                               Add a memory note (≤ 4000 chars).
  memory remove                DELETE /v1/host/openwop-app/projects/:id/memory/:noteId
                               Remove a memory note.
  schedules                    GET    /v1/host/openwop-app/projects/:id/schedules
                               Scheduled workflow runs for the project.
  schedules add                POST   /v1/host/openwop-app/projects/:id/schedules
                               Add a schedule (5-field cron).
  schedules update             PATCH  /v1/host/openwop-app/projects/:id/schedules/:jobId
                               Edit a schedule (--enabled / --no-enabled to toggle).
  schedules remove             DELETE /v1/host/openwop-app/projects/:id/schedules/:jobId
                               Remove a schedule.
  chat                         POST   /v1/host/openwop-app/projects/:id/chat
                               Ensure the project's group conversation exists (idempotent) and return its sessionId.

Project workspaces (host-extension). A project scopes members + knowledge + schedules;
`create` needs the owning --org. The host is the authority; the CLI mirrors + relays.
Reads need access to the project (private projects: members only); writes need
workspace:write in the project's org — membership alone never grants write.

Exit codes: 0 ok · 1 server error · 2 usage / not found / validation · 4 not signed in or not permitted.

Examples:
  openwop projects update p_1 --workflows wf.a,wf.b --charter '{"goal":"Ship v2","status":"active"}'
  openwop projects members add p_1 --ref agent:r_7 --role lead
  openwop projects knowledge documents add p_1 kc_1 --org o_1 --title Spec --file spec.pdf --content-type application/pdf
  openwop projects schedules add p_1 --cron-expr "0 9 * * 1" --workflow-id wf.weekly
  openwop projects chat p_1

Commerce promotions (host-extension /v1/host/openwop-app/promotions/…, org-scoped).
--type is one of cart_threshold | product_discount | loss_leader | tiered | bogo.
--reward is {"kind":"percentage"|"fixed","value":n}; --scope is
{"productIds":[…],"categories":[…],"all":true}; --bogo is {"buy":n,"get":m};
--budget is {"maxDiscount":n,"maxQuantity":n}. The host validates every rule
(a loss_leader needs budget.maxDiscount, a tiered one needs --min-quantity).

Flags take the host's field names in kebab-case (priceMinor → --price-minor).
Money amounts are passed through exactly, in the unit the host's field names
(e.g. priceMinor = cents, priceMajorUnits = whole units); the CLI never
computes a price or a total. `--body`/`--body-file` supply the
full JSON body; individual flags override keys in it.

      GET /v1/host/openwop-app/public-recommendations/:org/resolve  (public, no auth) — Resolve recommendations as an anonymous storefront visitor.

Product recommendations (host-extension /v1/host/openwop-app/recommendations/…,
org-scoped). --slot is pdp | cart | checkout | post_purchase | category | home |
oos_404; --source is bought_together | cross_sell | upsell | similar | trending;
--holdout-pct is the A/B holdout percentage. `resolve` previews what a slot
shows (optionally as --contact-id); `public resolve` hits the anonymous
storefront route and never sends credentials. Prices are the host's own values.

Flags take the host's field names in kebab-case (priceMinor → --price-minor).
Money amounts are passed through exactly, in the unit the host's field names
(e.g. priceMinor = cents, priceMajorUnits = whole units); the CLI never
computes a price or a total. `--body`/`--body-file` supply the
full JSON body; individual flags override keys in it.

permitted (HTTP 401/403) · 1 server error.

  openwop recommendations placements list --org org_1
  openwop recommendations placements create --org org_1 --slot pdp --source bought_together --holdout-pct 10
  openwop recommendations resolve --org org_1 --slot pdp --product-id prod_1 --limit 4
  openwop recommendations public resolve --org org_1 --slot home

help.stdout:
Usage:
  openwop roster list [--host] [--json]
  openwop roster get <rosterId> [--json]
  openwop roster create --persona <name> --agent-ref <agentId> [--agent-version <v> | --agent-channel <c>] [--workflow <id>]... [--label <text>] [--description <text>] [--disabled] [--avatar-url <url>] [--json]
  openwop roster update <rosterId> [--persona <name>] [--workflow <id>]... [--label <text>] [--description <text>] [--enabled|--disabled] [--avatar-url <url>] [--json]
  openwop roster delete <rosterId> [--yes]
  openwop roster activity <rosterId> [--limit <limit>] [--status <status>] [--json]
  openwop roster check <rosterId>

Every write also accepts --body <json> / --body-file <path> for the full request body (typed flags override it).

Endpoints:
  activity                     GET    /v1/host/openwop-app/roster/:rosterId/activity
                               Recent runs this standing agent initiated.
  check                        POST   /v1/host/openwop-app/roster/:rosterId/check
                               Run the agent's heartbeat now: pick the next runnable card (or report why not).


Agent roster (RFC 0086). A roster entry is a named, tenant-scoped standing
agent that owns a portfolio of workflows[]; its triggers compose RFC 0052
(schedules) + RFC 0083 (the durable trigger bridge), and a run it initiates
emits the content-free roster.run.initiated attribution event.

'list' reads the NORMATIVE roster (RFC 0086 / agent-roster.md §B):
GET /v1/agents/roster. The normative view carries only protocol-shaped entries
(the host may omit host-only entries such as advisors); when the host does not
serve it (404/405/501), or with --host, 'list' reads the host-extension
GET /v1/host/openwop-app/roster instead (--verbose names the path that answered).
With no credential, a v2 host refuses the normative read (401); 'list' then
shows the host's anonymous view from the alias and says so on stderr.
'get'/'create'/'update'/'delete' drive the host-extension surface
GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE /v1/host/openwop-app/roster[/{rosterId}].

  --host             (list) Read the full host-extension roster instead of the normative view.

  --persona <name>   The agent's display persona (required on create).
  --agent-ref <id>   The agentId this entry binds to (RFC 0002 AgentRef; required on create).
  --agent-version <v> | --agent-channel <c>   Pin the AgentRef to a version XOR a channel.
  --workflow <id>    A workflow in the entry's portfolio (repeatable).
  --label <text>     Short human label.
  --description <t>  Longer description.
  --enabled          (update) Re-enable the entry's triggers + heartbeat.
  --disabled         Create/leave the entry paused (triggers inert).
  --avatar-url <url> Photo URL for the entry.

Examples:
  openwop roster list
  openwop roster create --persona "Sally" --workflow sample.demo.triage --label "Support lead"
  openwop roster update r_123 --disabled
  openwop roster delete r_123 --yes

Sales territories (host-extension /v1/host/openwop-app/territories/…,
org-scoped). A model holds territories, assignment rules and quotas; build it
while it is in planning, then `models activate` (queues a review — activation
changes who can see which records) and `reassign` to re-run assignment.
Rules: --target company | deal, --filter is the server's filter expression
JSON. Quotas: --period YYYY-Qn or YYYY-MM, --amount with --currency (ISO-4217;
the server refuses an amount with no currency), --rep-splits
[{"subjectId":"…","amount":n}]. `quota set` writes the whole quota for that
period (there is no partial update).

Flags take the host's field names in kebab-case (priceMinor → --price-minor).
Money amounts are passed through exactly, in the unit the host's field names
(e.g. priceMinor = cents, priceMajorUnits = whole units); the CLI never
computes a price or a total. `--body`/`--body-file` supply the
full JSON body; individual flags override keys in it.

                               Merge-patch the migration journey (only sections you pass change; JSON null clears one). --stage key=pending|done (target, assess, map-data, map-boundaries, shadow-prove, cut-over).


Durable multi-agent orchestration at fleet scale (alias: `fleet`). A workforce is
a governed bundle — agent specs, graduated-autonomy posture, and aggregate
telemetry derived from its runs. `status` requests a cutover (the host gates
promotion to `production` on the workforce having graduated to bounded-autonomous,
and always allows rollback). `eval` runs a live shadow eval (host-gated capability).

This group COMPOSES with — and does not duplicate — `kanban` (task boards) and
`roster` (standing agents): it renders the workforce's governance/metrics view,
never re-modelling boards or roster entries. The host is the authority; the CLI
renders its resolved view and fails closed if the surface isn't advertised.

Endpoints:
  list        GET   /v1/host/openwop-app/workforces
  get         GET   /v1/host/openwop-app/workforces/{id}
  metrics     GET   /v1/host/openwop-app/workforces/{id}/metrics
  governance  GET   /v1/host/openwop-app/workforces/{id}/governance
  migration   GET   /v1/host/openwop-app/workforces/{id}/migration
  trace       GET   /v1/host/openwop-app/workforces/{id}/trace[?q=]
  shadow      GET   /v1/host/openwop-app/workforces/{id}/shadow
  status      PATCH /v1/host/openwop-app/workforces/{id}   (body {status})
  eval        POST  /v1/host/openwop-app/workforces/{id}/eval

  --q <query>   (trace) Match runs by correlationId / batchId / runId / outcome / status.
  --json        Print the raw host response instead of the rendered view.

Exit codes:
  reads / status / eval   0 ok · 2 usage · 1 not-found / not-eligible / error
